title: Prescriptions Controlled Substance Manual: Amount of the Controlled Decline Credit
content:
The controlled decline credit is the amount returned by the original payment method when a patient declines the open owed balance of a Kestrel Prescriptions record in the Schedule V Controlled Prescription, Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription or Schedule II Controlled Prescription class.

## Section 1 — The records used

The controlled short fill is the fill named by the prescription's most recent owed-balance entry, and the owed units are the units that entry booked. The patient pay and the units dispensed of the controlled short fill are read from the fill ledger.

## Section 2 — The credit

The controlled decline credit is the controlled short fill's patient pay multiplied by the owed units and divided by the controlled short fill's units dispensed plus the owed units, rounded to the nearest cent — once, on the credit as a whole.

## Worked figures (hypothetical controlled short fills)

| Patient pay | Units dispensed | Owed units | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18.00 | 40 | 20 | 18.00 multiplied by 20, divided by 60: 6.00 |
| 10.00 | 25 | 5 | 10.00 multiplied by 5, divided by 30: 1.6667, rounded to 1.67 |
| 9.00 | 10 | 20 | 9.00 multiplied by 20, divided by 30: 6.00 |

## Point of judgement

**The prescription shows an older owed-balance entry and a newer one.** The newer, most recent entry names the controlled short fill, and its booked units are the owed units.
